meta.coverage: coverage: core calculators [mpf, mtc, lpn] x core languages [es, pt, fr, tr] (in scope iff calculator OR language is core; identity strings always)
meta.notes: Translate only keys in keys_to_translate; preserve HTML, units, and symbols.
meta.placeholder_notes: A word in curly braces ({n}, {ids}, {flow}, {iterations}, {name}) is a PLACEHOLDER the page replaces at runtime. Keep every one of them, spelled exactly as in English, braces included. Never translate the word inside the braces. You MAY move a placeholder to wherever your language needs it in the sentence.
meta.control_name_notes: Where an English string names a control, it names it in one of two shapes. A single control is written as its label followed by the widget word: "press the Calculate button", "the Recalculate automatically setting", "the Required fire flow box". A menu path is written as comma-separated labels: "File, Save as"; "Settings, Calculation, Hydraulics". In BOTH shapes the label is another key's value. Translate it with exactly the words you used for that key, so the sentence still names what is on the screen; translate the widget word and the surrounding prose normally.
meta.context_notes: Use key_context.neighbors to keep register consistent with nearby translated strings.
meta.syn_notes: Use key_syn when present; these entries provide terse disambiguation comments only where translation risk exists.
meta.suggestion_box_notes: Read suggestion_box and follow it. It is part of your instructions, not a footnote: a sprint does not close while a translator complaint is unanswered.
meta.concept_notes: Read concept_source and follow it. key_concepts lists, for a key that names a defined concept, the definition you translate from; English is one rendering of it.

suggestion_box:
## Suggestion box — file a grievance about the English

If any English string made you guess, file it. You are the only person who will ever
notice, and a string that made you guess will make the next 25 translators guess too.

File an entry when: the English has more than one plausible reading; a verb or adjective
has no stated object; a word's intended sense is not its most common sense; a term maps
onto a dangerous second sense in your language; a claim in the text looks false or stale;
or the tooling handed you a preferred_translation that is wrong for the context.

Report them in your final message as a JSON array, separate from your prose:

FRICTION: [
  {"key": "<lang key>", "complaint": "<what made you guess, in one sentence>",
   "readings": ["<reading you chose>", "<reading you rejected>"]}
]

An empty array is a fine and useful answer. Do NOT invent entries -- a false one costs a
human's attention. But do not stay quiet to be agreeable either: this channel exists
because real complaints were previously buried in prose and never acted on.

Where it goes and what happens next: the orchestrator copies each entry into
dev/english-friction/<sprint>.json, adds "source": "translator" and "lang": "<your
language code>", and answers it with a "disposition" plus a written "resolution" --
english (the English was rewritten), intent, glossary, dismissed (with the reason), or
refer-to-human. refer-to-human is a real answer and does NOT close the entry: escalating
is not resolving, and it stays visible until Tom rules on it. friction_check.php blocks
the sprint from CLOSING while any entry of yours is unanswered, so filing one is expected
work that the sprint waits on -- not a complaint about the sprint.
concept_source:
## Concepts are the source

Where key_concepts lists a concept for a key, its definition is the authoritative source
and the English string is one rendering of it: translate the thing the definition
describes, and give that concept the same word in every key that cites it, a word no
neighbouring concept in the definition shares. Where a key has no key_concepts entry,
the English is the source, as before.

prompt_context_by_prefix.mtc:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): portata
    MEANS: The volume of water passing a cross-section per unit time (Q). A rate, not a movement: it is not velocity (speed at a point) and not a general word for water moving.
- velocity (v): velocità
    MEANS: The speed of water through a cross-section: flow divided by the flow area (v). A speed, not a rate of volume, so it is not flow.
- hydraulic radius (R_h): raggio idraulico
    MEANS: Flow area divided by wetted perimeter (R_h), a length. Not the geometric radius of a pipe: for a full circular pipe it is one quarter of the diameter.
- wetted perimeter (P_w): perimetro bagnato
    MEANS: The length of channel or pipe boundary in contact with the water in one cross-section (P_w). Excludes the free water surface.
- Manning roughness (n): coefficiente di scabrezza di Manning
    MEANS: The empirical boundary roughness coefficient n in the Manning formula. A property of the channel or pipe surface, not a height of roughness and not the Darcy-Weisbach friction factor or the Hazen-Williams C.
- slope (S): pendenza
    MEANS: Vertical change divided by horizontal distance (S), dimensionless or in percent. Used for a channel bed, a pipe and a friction (energy) slope. Never an incline for walking or running.
    DO NOT render as: activity/fitness sense of 'grade' — the treadmill or trail incline for running/walking/jogging; this is the hydraulic energy gradient, not an exercise setting; geographic or topographic landform term; school grade / academic mark
- specific gravity (sg): densità relativa
    MEANS: The dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (sg). Not a weight and not a force.
    DO NOT render as: attaching units to the value — it is a dimensionless ratio (≈2.65 for rock); a weight-flavored term is fine but the QUANTITY never carries units; a non-standard or transliterated coinage — use each language's own dominant, culturally-standard term for this concept, whatever its literal parts; we do not judge terminology, culture does
- median rock size (D50): diametro mediano dei massi
    MEANS: The rock particle size for which half the rock by weight is finer (D50).

mtc.definition: The volume of water passing a cross-section per unit time (Q). A rate, not a movement: it is not velocity (speed at a point) and not a general word for water moving.
mtc.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
mtc.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed). | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] Counted in the shipped strings, 100 English sites. The glossary rendering is the majority in every language that has one: hr protok 85, sr проток 84, cs průtok 79, ru расход 76, fr débit 75, pt vazão 73, zh 流量 72, bg водно количество 70, km លំហូរ 70, es caudal 69, it portata 69, ar تدفق 69, id debit 69, de Durchfluss 68, tr debi 64, fa دبی 58, he ספיקה 43, uk витрата 43 sites of 99. A second, general water-flowing word still stands at some of the rest: fa جریان 37, id aliran 27, es flujo 25, he זרימה 21, tr akış 20, fr écoulement 15, ar جريان 15, pt escoamento 14, it deflusso 12. NOT ALL OF THOSE ARE DEFECTS -- some English sites really do describe water flowing rather than naming Q, and a count cannot tell the two apart. A worklist for a term-centric sweep, not a correction list.

mtc.definition: The speed of water through a cross-section: flow divided by the flow area (v). A speed, not a rate of volume, so it is not flow.
mtc.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

mtc.definition: Flow area divided by wetted perimeter (R_h), a length. Not the geometric radius of a pipe: for a full circular pipe it is one quarter of the diameter.
mtc.context: Cross-sectional flow area divided by wetted perimeter. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used the Latin loanword 'hidraulički radijus' — this form is widely used in South Slavic engineering practice and may be more recognizable to field practitioners than the native Slavic equivalents 'полупречник' (sr) / 'polumjer' (hr). Both are correct; native Slavic engineers may encounter both forms. DATA-ERROR FIX 2026-07-10 (category-3 sw wave-3 sprint): previous sw value 'radius ya maji' (literally 'radius of water', English loanword 'radius' + 'of water') named the substance rather than the hydraulic-geometry property, and did not read as an engineering term. Changed to 'radiasi ya kihaidroliki' (radius + 'hydraulic', adjectival ki- form), matching the '[radius] + hydraulic' construction used by fr/de/it/es/ro/tr (rayon hydraulique / hydraulischer Radius / raggio idraulico / radio hidráulico / raza hidraulică / hidrolik yarıçap). Used in lib/lang.ec.sw.php's mpf_hydraulic_radius.

mtc.definition: The length of channel or pipe boundary in contact with the water in one cross-section (P_w). Excludes the free water surface.
mtc.context: Length of the channel or pipe boundary in contact with flowing water. Appears in Manning calculators.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1682 confirms: es = 'perímetro mojado', fr = 'périmètre mouillé'. Use the standard hydraulic engineering phrase. 'Wetted' here means 'in contact with water', not 'soaked'. Pre-2026 sr human used 'okvašeni obim' (obim = natural South Slavic word for perimeter/circumference); current uses 'квашени периметар' (периметар = Greek-derived loanword). Both are correct; 'obim/opseg' is more natural in informal Serbian/Croatian field use. Task 109 stages 4 & 5 (2026-07-19): bg wrong-word 'навлажнен' (moistened) corrected to 'омокрен' in mpf_wetted_perimeter (stage 4) and cs_notes_3_def (stage 5); km គ្រែទឹក (water bed) also confirmed corrected to glossary បរិវេណសើម (stage 4).

mtc.definition: The empirical boundary roughness coefficient n in the Manning formula. A property of the channel or pipe surface, not a height of roughness and not the Darcy-Weisbach friction factor or the Hazen-Williams C.
mtc.context: Manning's n — empirical roughness coefficient used in the Manning formula for open-channel and pipe flow.
mtc.translation_notes: Always include 'Manning' as a proper noun. The coefficient itself (n) needs no translation — only the label does. Do not translate as generic 'roughness coefficient' without 'Manning'. TYPO FIX 2026-07-09 (category-3 wave-1 sprint): ru/uk transliterations were single-н 'Манинга'/'Манінга', flagged by the ru wave-1 agent as inconsistent with the established double-н transliteration ('Маннинга'/'Маннінга') used 11+ times elsewhere in both lang files (predates this sprint). Corrected to double-н for consistency. Task 109 stage 4 (2026-07-19): am 3-way 'roughness' spelling drift standardized to file-dominant ሻካሪነት (was ሻካርነት); it confirmed on scabrezza and sw on usuguo (both already glossary-correct). [2026-07-24] he corrected: was transliterated 'מנינג'; shipped lang.ec.he.php uses Latin 'Manning' throughout (mi_/mpf_/mphl_ menus), so glossary now matches file practice.

mtc.definition: Vertical change divided by horizontal distance (S), dimensionless or in percent. Used for a channel bed, a pipe and a friction (energy) slope. Never an incline for walking or running.
mtc.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
mtc.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses. | [2026-08-25, glossary_rendering_census.php] 16 English sites. Most of what a census reports as a rival here is the SIDE SLOPE of a channel, a different concept and correct where it stands: fr talus 5, zh 边坡 5, de böschung 4, ru откос 4, it scarpata 4, ar الجانبي 4. Three are genuine splits inside one language: ur ships ڈھلان at 14 sites while this entry holds ڈھلوان, used at 1; hi ships ढलान 10 against ढाल 5; ps ships میل 9 against شیب 6. ro is a diacritic split only -- pantă here, panta at 4 sites.

mtc.definition: The dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (sg). Not a weight and not a force.
mtc.context: Dimensionless ratio of a material's density to the density of water (≈2.65 for crushed granite/basalt; Robinson valid range 2.54–2.82). Appears in Rock Chute Design and Manning Trapezoidal Channel. The English source keeps "specific gravity" — the standard English term and the one Robinson's paper uses (rc_ cites it). We deliberately do NOT swap it for "relative density" even though that reads as more modern: per Tom's principle (2026-07-20) we defer to each language's own dominant standard term rather than judging terminology.
mtc.translation_notes: [2026-07-20 RESOLUTION — Tom's principle: 'we are not the judges of terminology, culture is.'] Use each language's dominant, culturally-standard term for this dimensionless concept, whatever its literal composition. A weight-flavored STANDARD term is CORRECT, not an error to be reformed toward 'relative density': tr 'özgül ağırlık', he 'משקל סגולי' (standard Hebrew physics-curriculum term), sr 'специфична тежина', ps 'ځانګړی ثقل' are the established local standards and stay. The ONLY hard rule is physical — the value is a dimensionless ratio and never carries units. hr RESOLVED to 'relativna gustoća', the dominant modern Croatian standard (gustoća = density), matching the shipped file; the glossary was the stale side. sw 'uzito maalum' is NOT an auto-defect: if it is the standard Swahili term for the concept used dimensionlessly (parallel to Turkish özgül ağırlık), it is correct — confirm it is the Swahili standard, do not replace it with a coined 'relative density' calque. This supersedes the earlier 'weight-word exception' framing, which wrongly implied 'relative density' was the target to push. [2026-07-21 assessment] Two more glossary values were stale vs. their shipped, internally-consistent files (same class as hr): sr updated 'специфична тежина'→'релативна густина' and it 'peso specifico relativo'→'densità relativa' to match each file's actual standard usage; no lang-file change needed. (Historical: de 'spezifisches Gewicht'→'relative Dichte' and ru 'удельный вес'→'относительная плотность' were corrected in the 2026-07-08 category-1 QA — those were genuine non-standard-in-context values, not the same as a language whose actual standard is weight-flavored.) [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] 'Density relative to water' definitional tip now ships in all 26 languages on mtc_sgrock/rc_sg. NEW cross-key LABEL drift found (distinct from the glossary-vs-file staleness above): within a single language the two calculators disagree on the SG term — mtc_sgrock uses a weight-flavored label while rc_sg uses a relative-density-flavored one — in pt (Gravidade específica vs Densidade relativa), uk (Питома вага vs Відносна густина), ar (الكثافة النوعية vs الكثافة النسبية), fa (وزن مخصوص نسبی vs چگالی نسبی); sr already noted. Both labels are individually defensible per the cultural-standard rule, but the intra-language inconsistency between the two calculators warrants a future authorized label-consolidation pass. Tips were translated tip-only, labels preserved. [2026-07-21 Task 133 RESOLVED] Authorized label-consolidation pass done: in each affected language mtc_sgrock's divergent weight-flavored label was aligned to rc_sg's relative-density-flavored label (which already matched this entry's dominant-standard translation) — pt→'Densidade relativa da rocha', uk→'Відносна густина каменю', ar→'الكثافة النسبية للصخور', fa→'چگالی نسبی سنگ', sr→'Релативна густина камена'. Both calculators now agree within each language (ar retains a pre-existing singular/plural difference on the rock word only — للصخور vs للصخر — the SG term itself is aligned). Tips untouched (already consistent). Note: this consolidation aligned toward relative-density because rc_sg happened to hold the standard in all 5; it does NOT contradict the cultural-standard rule (a weight-flavored standard like tr/he/sr's own would be equally valid to consolidate toward where it is the dominant term).

mtc.definition: The rock particle size for which half the rock by weight is finer (D50).
mtc.context: The particle size at which 50% of the rock is finer by weight. The primary output of the Robinson rock chute method. Also used in Manning Trapezoidal Channel riprap sizing. The symbol D50 is universal — translate only the descriptive label.
mtc.translation_notes: D50 (or D₅₀) is a universal engineering symbol — do not translate it. Translate only the label 'median rock size' or 'median particle size'. Most languages express this as 'median diameter'. Do not use 'average' (average ≠ median statistically). Spanish: 'tamaño mediano de roca'. French: 'taille médiane des rochers'. Chinese: '中值粒径'. **2026-07-13 cross-language research pass (item 44):** researched whether 'average/mean'-register wording (found in several languages' initial translations) is a real engineering error or defensible practice-register, using web research into each language's actual geotechnical/sedimentology literature. Confirmed real errors, corrected in both the lang files and this glossary: de ('mittlere'→'mediane'/'medianer', citing German BAW government sedimentology usage), cs ('střední'→'mediánová', citing Charles University hydraulics course), ru ('средний'→'медианный' for mi_d50in; rc_D50 already correct), tr ('orta'→'ortanca', matching the term already correct in rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), fa ('متوسط'→'میانه', citing Persian percentile-based technical definitions), ur ('اوسط'/'درمیانی'/'درمیانہ'→'وسیط', mirroring Arabic's وسيط/متوسط distinction), sr ('средња'→'медијанска', matching mi_d50in which already used 'Медијана'). Found already correct in the lang files (glossary was simply stale, not the file — see item 42): bg ('медианен размер', confirmed live in mi_d50in/rc_D50/rc_notes_1_def), uk ('медіанний розмір'), hr ('medijalna veličina', an adjective form of medijan/medijana), ro ('dimensiunea mediană'). One language, am (Amharic), was researched and found to have no distinct circulating median-vs-average term at all — even Amharic dictionaries gloss 'median' as 'መካከለኛ' (same word used for 'middle/average') — so 'የድንጋይ መካከለኛ መጠን' was left unchanged; there's no more-correct term available in practice.
